cases.prompt: Review this diff together with the repo it lands in — I want the surrounding handlers and components checked too.
expected: Repo scanned in full plus the diff; the existing ReleaseNotes component is flagged medium (dangerouslySetInnerHTML); gate passes; every scanned file appears in the threat-model record
Finding: mass assignment — the whole FormData is spread into the update, so a user can set role or tenant_id; traced from actions.ts formData → update on profiles
Rates it via reachability × impact (any authenticated user; privilege escalation or tenant move) as High or Critical, with an exploit sketch
Fix in code: zod schema allow-listing display_name and avatar_url, plus a negative regression test that tries to set role and fails before the fix
Also notes the RLS update policy should have a with check that prevents role/tenant changes

cases.prompt: PR #88 adds app/api/preview/route.ts: GET ?url=... fetches the URL server-side and returns the page title for link cards. Any authenticated user can call it. Review it.
expected: Finding: SSRF — user-controlled URL fetched server-side, traced from the query param in route.ts to fetch()
Impact includes reaching internal/metadata endpoints; severity derived from reachability R2 × impact, with an exploit sketch (e.g. internal address)
Fix: allow-listed hosts or blocking private/link-local ranges after DNS resolution, timeouts, no redirects to internal hosts, plus a negative test

cases.prompt: Quick review: this PR adds NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to .env.example and uses it in lib/supabaseAdmin.ts, which is imported by a client component for an admin dashboard.
expected: Critical finding: the service-role key is exposed in the client bundle via the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, bypassing RLS for anyone (R3 × I3)
Fix: move the key to server-only env without NEXT_PUBLIC_, use the admin client only in server code behind an authz guard, and rotate the exposed key
Gate fails: the review is not approved while the Critical remains

cases.prompt:
Review this Supabase function added in a migration:
```sql
create function search_orders(q text) returns setof orders language plpgsql security definer as $$
begin
  return query execute 'select * from orders where note ilike ''%' || q || '%''';
end $$;
```
Called from app/api/search/route.ts with the user's query string.
expected: Finding: SQL injection via string-concatenated dynamic SQL, traced route.ts query param → rpc → execute
Flags security definer as an RLS bypass that lets the query read every tenant's orders
Fix: parameterised query (format with %L or USING / plain SQL), security invoker, and a negative regression test; rated Critical

cases.prompt: New endpoint GET /api/files/[id] looks up storage path by id with the admin client and streams the file. Users are in tenants; files belong to tenants. Ship it?
expected: Finding: IDOR / cross-tenant read — the id is not checked against the session's tenant and the admin client bypasses RLS
Trace from the route param through the lookup to storage (entry → lookup → admin client → storage), rated Critical (R2 × I3)
Fix: cookie-bound RLS client (or an explicit tenant-from-session check), plus a negative test where tenant B requests tenant A's file id

cases.prompt: PR adds comments to tickets. Comment body is stored raw and rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: marked(body)}} in components/Comment.tsx. Comments are visible to everyone in the tenant. Review.
expected: Finding: stored XSS, traced from the comment insert to dangerouslySetInnerHTML in Comment.tsx
Severity by rubric (authenticated user, impact on other users in the tenant e.g. session actions) with an exploit sketch
Fix: sanitise the rendered HTML (e.g. DOMPurify) or render markdown without raw HTML, plus a regression test with a script payload
